spans.s:
मृग् मृग् (more properly to be regarded
as a Nom. fr. मृग), cl. 4. P., 10. A.
मृग्यति, मृगयते (ep. also P. -ति), &c., to
chase, hunt, pursue; to seek, search for, seek after;
to investigate, examine; to strive for, aim at; to
visit; to desire or request or beg anything (acc.)
from another (abl., gen., or with सकाशात्); अन्तर्
मृग्, to examine or investigate inwardly, i. e. in
the mind: Pass. मृग्यते, to be searched or sought
after, to be pursued.

मृग, अस्, m. a wild beast; an animal in general,
any quadruped, a deer, stag, antelope, musk-deer;
game in general; the spots on the moon represented
as a hare or antelope; the celestial antelope or the
Nakṣatra Mṛga-śiras; the sign of the zodiac Ca-
pricorn (or the tenth arc of 30° in a circle); an
elephant characterized by particular marks (one of
the three classes of elephants); a particular kind of
large bird (Ved.); epithet of a demon or of Vṛtra
in the form of a deer slain by Indra (Ved.); N. of a
celestial being or tutelary divinity occupying a parti-
cular place in an astrological house divided into eighty-
one compartments (Ved.); epithet of a particular
class of men whose conduct in coitus resembles that
of the roebuck; N. of the district in Śāka-dvīpa
inhabited principally by Brāhmans, (also read मङ्ग,
cf. मग); = मृग-नाभि, musk; the month Mār-
gaśīrṣa; a particular Aja-pāla sacrifice; seeking,
search (= मार्गण); pursuit, hunting, chase; re-
search, inquiry, investigation; asking, soliciting, beg-
ging; (ई), f. a female deer or antelope, doe; N. of
the mythical progenitress of the antelopes; epithet
of a particular class of women; a particular metre,
four times ¯˘¯; demoniacal possession, epilepsy.
—मृग-काक, औ, m. du. a deer and a crow.
—मृग-कानन, अम्, n. a forest abounding in
game; a park, preserve; [cf. मृगारण्य, मृ-
गया-वन.]
—मृग-क्षीर, अम्, n. antelope's
milk, doe's milk.
—मृग-गामिनी, f. a kind of
medicinal substance (= विडङ्गा).
—मृग-ग्र-
हण, अम्, n. the capture of a deer.
—मृग-चर्-
मीय, अस्, m., N. of an author.
—मृग-चर्या, f.
the acting like a deer (a kind of penance, see मृग-
चारिन् below).
—मृग-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, acting like
a deer (as certain devotees; cf. गो-चारिन्, which
appears to mean ‘acting like a cow, using the mouth
instead of the hands’).
—मृग-चैटक, अस्, m. (?),
a wild cat, pole-cat.
—मृग-जम्बुक, औ, m. du.
a deer and a jackal.
—मृग-जल, अम्, n. ‘deer-
water,’ mirage; see मृग-तृष्.
—मृगजल-
स्नान, अम्, n. bathing in the unreal waters of a
mirage, (a term for any impossibility.)
—मृग-जाति,
अयस्, f. pl. the deer species, whole race of deer.
—मृग-जालिका, f. a net for snaring game.
—मृग-
जीवन, अस्, m. one who lives by hunting, a hunter,
huntsman.
—मृग-तीर्थ, अम्, n., Ved. ‘animal
track,’ epithet of the path by which the priests at
the end of the Savana leave the sacred place to attend
to their bodily wants.
—मृग-तृष्, ट्, or मृग-
तृषा, or मृग-तृष्णा, or मृग-तृष्णि, इस्, or
[]
मृग-तृष्णिका, f. ‘deer-thirst,’ mirage, vapour
floating over sands or deserts, fancied appearance of
water in deserts.
—मृग-तोय, अम्, n. the water
of a mirage.
—मृग-त्व, अम्, n. the being a deer
or antelope, the state or condition of a deer.
—मृग-
दंश or मृग-दंशक, अस्, m. ‘animal-biter,’
a hunting-dog, dog.
—मृग-दाव, अस्, m. a wood
for game, park, preserve.
—मृग-दृश्, क्, f. ‘deer-
eyed,’ a woman with eyes like an antelope's; (क्),
m. the sign of the zodiac Capricorn.
—मृग-द्युत्,
त्, त्, त् (see 1. द्युत्, p. 437), attacking a deer, a
hunter.
—मृग-द्यू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, delighting or tak-
ing pleasure in deer; (ऊस्), m. a hunter.
—मृग-
द्विज, आस्, m. pl. beasts and birds.
—मृग-धर,
अस्, m. ‘bearing deer-like marks,’ the moon (which,
according to the Hindūs, is spotted like a deer or a
hare); N. of a minister of Prasena-jit.
—मृग-
धूम, N. of a Tīrtha.
—मृग-धूर्त or मृग-
धूर्तक, अस्, m. ‘animal-deceiver,’ a jackal.
—मृ-
ग-नयना, f. a fawn-eyed woman.
—मृग-नाभि,
इस्, m. ‘deer's navel,’ musk; a musk-deer; [cf.
नाभि.]
—मृगनाभि-जा, f. musk.
—मृगनाभि-
मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of musk.
—मृग-निर्मोक-वसन, अस्, आ, अम्, clothed in
the cast-off skin of a deer.
—मृग-नेत्र, अस्, आ,
अम्, having the Nakṣatra Mṛga for a leader, re-
lating to this Nakṣatra; (आ), f. ‘fawn-eyed,’ a woman
with eyes like an antelope's.
—मृग-पक्षिन्,
इणस्, m. pl. beasts and birds.
—मृग-पति, इस्, m.
‘lord of the beasts,’ a lion; a tiger; a roebuck.
—मृग-पद, अम्, n. a deer's foot, deer's track
(= मृग्याः पदम्).
—मृग-पालिका, f. a musk-
deer.
—मृग-पिप्लु, उस्, m. ‘deer-marked,’ the
moon.
—मृग-पोत or मृग-पोतक, अस्, m. a
young deer, fawn.
—मृग-प्रभु, उस्, m. ‘lord
of the beasts,’ the lion.
—मृग-प्रेक्षिन्, ई, इणी,
इ, looking at (anything) like a deer, having the eyes
of a deer; [cf. वृक-प्˚.]
—मृग-बधाजीव
(˚ध-आज्˚), अस्, m. ‘living by killing deer,’ a deer-
killer, hunter.
—मृग-बन्धिनी, f. a net for snar-
ing game or for confining deer.
—मृग-बालक,
अस्, m. a young deer.
—मृग-भक्षा, f. Nardo-
stachys Jatamansi.
—मृग-भोजनी, f. coloquintida,
colocynth, bitter apple.
—मृग-मद, अस्, m.
musk.
—मृगमद-वासा, f. a musk-bag.
—मृ-
ग-मन्द, अस्, m. epithet of a class of elephants;
(आ), f. the mythical progenitress of lions, Sṛmaras,
and Camaras; [cf. मृग-वती.]
—मृग-मन्द्र,
अस्, m. epithet of a class of elephants.
—मृग-
मय, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from or consisting of
wild animals.
—मृग-मांस, अम्, n. deer's flesh,
venison.
—मृग-मातृका, f. a species of wild
animal; a doe.
—मृग-मास, अस्, m. the month
Mārgaśīrṣa.
—मृग-मुख, अस्, m. the sign of
the zodiac Capricorn; [cf. मृगास्य.]
—मृग-
यूथ, अम्, n. a herd of deer.
—मृगयूथ-प,
अस्, m. lord of the herd of deer.
—मृग-रसा, f. a
species of plant (= मृगादनी, सह-देवी).
—मृ-
ग-राज्, ट्, m. ‘king of the beasts,’ a lion, the sign
of the zodiac Leo; a tiger.
—मृग-राज, अस्, m.
‘king of the beasts,’ a lion, the sign of the zodiac
Leo; a tiger; the moon.
—मृगराज-धारिन्, ई,
m. (probably) the moon; ‘lion-shaped,’ the sign of
the zodiac Leo.
—मृगराज-लक्ष्मन्, आ, आ, अ,
‘characterized by the lion (or the moon),’ bearing
that surname (= सिंह-चिह्न).
—मृग-राटिका, f.
a species of medicinal plant (= जीवन्ती).
—मृग-
रिपु, उस्, m. ‘the enemy of wild animals,’ the lion.
—मृग-रूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘deer-shaped,’ being in
the form of an antelope.
—मृग-रोम-ज, अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘produced from animal's hair,’ woollen.
—मृ-
ग-लक्ष्मन्, आ, or मृग-लाञ्छन, अस्, m.
‘spotted like a deer,’ the moon.
—मृगलाञ्छन-
ज, अस्, m. ‘son of the moon,’ the planet Mercury.
—मृग-लेखा, f. the deer-like streak on the moon.
—मृग-लोचन, अस्, m. ‘deer-eyed,’ the moon;
(आ or ई), f. a woman with eyes like an antelope's.
—मृग-वती, f., N. of the mythical progenitress
of the bears and Sṛmaras.
—मृग-वधाजीव
(˚ध-आज्˚), अस्, m. ‘one who lives by killing wild
animals,’ a huntsman.
—मृग-वन, अम्, n. a forest
[]
abounding in wild animals, a park, preserve.
—मृ-
गवन-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-
place on the Narmadā river.
—मृग-वल्लभ, अस्,
m. ‘liked by deer,’ a species of grass (= कुन्दर),
—मृग-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘having a deer for a
vehicle,’ epithet of Vāyu, god of the wind (who is
sometimes represented mounted on an antelope),
air, wind.
—मृग-वीथी, f. ‘deer-track,’ an epithet
of that portion of the moon's course which includes
the constellations Śravaṇā, Śata-bhiṣaj, and Pūrva-
bhadra-padā; [cf. मृगाख्य.]
—मृग-वैणिक,
अम्, n. epithet of a particular posture in sitting.
—मृग-व्याध, अस्, m. a hunter of wild animals,
huntsman; the dog-star or Sirius; an epithet of
Śiva; N. of one of the eleven Rudras.
—मृग-
व्याध-सर्प-शूकर, आस्, m. pl. the deer, hunter,
snake, and boar.
—मृग-व्याधीय, अस्, आ, अम्,
relating to the hunter and the deer.
—मृग-
व्याल-निषेवित, अस्, आ, अम्, infested by wild beasts
and serpents.
—मृग-शायिका, f. the lying or re-
clining posture of an antelope (e. g. शयीत मृग-
शायिकाम्, let him lie as still as an antelope).
—मृ-
ग-शाव, अस्, m. a young deer, fawn.
—मृग-
शावक, अस्, m. = मृग-शाव.
—मृगशावाक्ष
(˚व-अक्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, ‘fawn-eyed,’ having eyes
like those of a young deer or fawn.
—मृग-
शिर, अस्, आ, m. f. the Nakṣatra Mṛga-śiras, (see
नक्षत्र.)
—मृग-शिरस्, अस्, n., N. of the tenth
or, according to some, third or fifth Nakṣatra or
lunar mansion (containing three stars, one of which
is λ Orionis and figured by an antelope's head; see
नक्षत्र); (आस्, आस्, अस्), born under the Nakṣatra
Mṛga-śiras; (आस्), m., scil. हस्त, a particular posi-
tion of the hands.
—मृग-शीर्ष, अम्, n. the con-
stellation Mṛga-śiras, (according to some also अस्, आ,
m. f.); (अस्, आ, अम्), born under the constellation Mṛga-
śiras; (अस्), m., scil. मास, the month Mārgaśīrṣa;
scil. हस्त, epithet of a particular position of the
hands, (also मृग-शीर्षक.)
—मृग-शीर्षन्, आ,
m. the constellation Mṛga-śiras.
—मृग-शूकर,
औ, m. du. a deer and a boar.
—मृग-शृङ्ग, अम्,
n. a stag's horn.
—मृग-शृङ्ग-व्रतिन्, इनस्, m.
pl., N. of a particular sect.
—मृग-श्रेष्ठ, अस्,
m. ‘best of beasts, chief of animals,’ a tiger.
—मृ-
ग-सक्थ, अम्, n. = मृगस्य सक्थि, Pāṇ.

.
—मृग-सत्तम, अस्, m. the best of antelopes.
—मृग-सत्त्र, अम्, n., Ved., N. of a festival
lasting nineteen days.
—मृग-हन्, आ, m. ‘deer-
slayer,’ a huntsman.
—मृगाक्षी (˚ग-अक्˚), f. a
fawn-eyed woman, a woman with eyes like an ante-
lope's; coloquintida, colocynth; = त्रि-यामा.
—मृ-
गाखर (˚ग-आख्˚), अस्, m., Ved. the lair or den
of a wild beast, the hole of any wild animal.
—मृ-
गाख्य (˚ग-आख्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, named after the
deer, (मृगाख्या, वीथी, a portion of the moon's
course which comprises three constellations beginning
with Maitra.)
—मृगाङ्क (˚ग-अङ्˚), अस्, m. ‘deer-
spotted, spotted like a deer,’ the moon; camphor;
the wind [cf. मृग-वाहन]; N. of a sword (in
Kathā-sarit-s.

); of a man.
—मृगाङ्क-दत्त,
अस्, m., N. of a son of Amara-datta (king of Ayodhyā);
of the father of Aruṇa-datta.
—मृगाङ्कदत्तीय,
अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Mṛgāṅka-datta.
—मृ-
गाङ्क-रस, अस्, m. epithet of a kind of formula.
—मृगाङ्क-लेखा, f., N. of the daughter of a
king of the Vidyā-dharas.
—मृगाङ्क-वती, f., N.
of the wife of Dharma-dhvaja, king of Ujjayinī; of
the wife of Mṛgāṅka-sena.
—मृगाङ्क-सेन, अस्,
m., N. of a king of the Vidyā-dharas.
—मृगाङ्-
गना (˚ग-अङ्˚), f. a female deer, doe.
—मृगाजिन
(˚ग-अज्˚), अम्, n. a deer-skin.
—मृगाजीव (˚ग-
आज्˚), अस्, m. ‘subsisting by wild animals,’ a hunts-
man; a hyena.
—मृगाटवी (˚ग-अट्˚), f. = मृग-
कानन, q. v.
—मृगाण्ड-जा (˚ग-अण्˚), f. musk.
—मृगाद् (˚ग-अद्), त्, m. ‘animal-devourer,’ a
tiger.
—मृगादन (˚ग-अद्˚), अस्, m. ‘animal-
devourer,’ a hyena; a hunting leopard; (ई), f. colo-
quintida, colocynth (= इन्द्र-वारुणी).
—मृगा-
धिप (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m. ‘king of animals,’ a lion.
—मृगाधिपत्य (˚ग-आध्˚), अम्, n. dominion
over wild animals.
—मृगाधिराज (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्,
[]
m. = मृगाधिप.
—मृगान्तक (˚ग-अन्˚), अस्,
m. ‘animal-destroyer,’ a cheeta or hunting leopard.
—मृगाराति (˚ग-अर्˚), इस्, m. ‘enemy of wild
animals,’ a lion; a dog.
—मृगारि (˚ग-अरि), इस्, m.
‘enemy of wild animals,’ a lion; a tiger; a dog,
hound; a species of Moringa with red blossoms (=
रक्त-शिग्रु; cf. मार्गार).
—मृगा-वती, f., N. of
Dākṣāyaṇī on the Yamunā; N. of several princesses.
—मृगावती-चरित्र, अम्, n., N. of a work.
—मृ-
गाविध् (˚ग-आव्˚), त्, m. a deer-killer, huntsman.
—मृगास्य (˚ग-आस्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘deer-faced,’
having the head or face of an antelope; (अस्), m.
the sign of the zodiac Capricorn; [cf. मृग-
मुख.]
—मृगी-कुण्ड, N. of a Tīrtha.
—मृगी-
त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a female deer
or doe.
—मृगी-दृश्, क्, f. ‘deer-eyed, fawn-eyed,’
a woman with eyes like an antelope's.
—मृगी-
पति, इस्, m. ‘husband of Mṛgī,’ an epithet of
Kṛṣṇa.
—मृगी-लोचना, f. ‘fawn-eyed,’ a woman
with eyes like an antelope's.
—मृगेक्षण (˚ग-
ईक्˚), अम्, n. the eye of an antelope or fawn, an eye
like a deer's (आ), f. ‘fawn-eyed,’ a woman with
eyes like an antelope's coloquintida, colocynth.
—मृगेन्द्र (˚ग-इन्˚), अस्, m. ‘king of beasts,’ a
lion; the sign of the zodiac Leo; a tiger; a parti-
cular metre, four times ˘¯˘; N. of an author;
(अम्), n., N. of Mṛgendra's work; of a Tantra.
—मृगेन्द्र-चटक, अस्, m. a hawk, falcon.
—मृगेन्द्र-ता, f. lordship over the beasts, do-
minion over wild animals.
—मृगेन्द्र-मुख,
अम्, n. a lion's mouth; a particular metre, four times
˘˘˘˘¯˘˘¯˘¯˘¯¯.
—मृगेन्द्र-वृषभ,
औ, m. du. a lion and a bull.
—मृगेन्द्राणी, f.
Gendarussa Vulgaris (= अटरूषक; cf. सिंही).
—मृगेन्द्रासन (˚र-आस्˚), अम्, n. ‘lion's seat,’
a throne; [cf. सिंहासन.]
—मृगेन्द्रास्य (˚र-
आस्˚), अस्, m. ‘lion-faced,’ an epithet of Śiva.
—मृगेर्वारु (˚ग-इर्˚), coloquintida, colocynth;
a species of animal; a white deer (?).
—मृगेर्वा-
रुक (˚ग-इर्˚), a species of animal (said to dwell
in holes or caves).
—मृगेश्वर (˚ग-ईश्˚), अस्, m.
‘lord of beasts,’ a lion; the sign of the zodiac Leo.
—मृगेष्ट (˚ग-इष्˚), अस्, m. a species of jasmine.
—मृगैर्वारु or मृगैर्वारुक (˚ग-एर्˚) =
मृगेर्वारु.
—मृगोत्तम (˚ग-उत्˚), अस्, m. best
of antelopes, a beautiful antelope or deer; (अम्), n.
the Nakṣatra Mṛga-śiras.
—मृगोत्तमाङ्ग (˚ग-
उत्˚), अम्, n. ‘antelope-head,’ the Nakṣatra Mṛga-
śiras.

मृगणा, f. seeking, searching, search, investiga-
tion, research, inquiry.
मृगण्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. hunting wild animals.

मृगमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, seeking, pursuing, hunt-
ing.

मृगय, अस्, m., Ved. N. of a demon conquered
by Indra; [cf. मृग.]

मृगया, f. hunting, the chase; the Chase per-
sonified as one of the attendants of Revanta.
—मृ-
गया-यान, अम्, n. the going out to hunt, a hunting
expedition.
—मृगयारण्य (˚या-अर्˚) or मृगया-
वन, अम्, n. a forest prepared or suited for hunting,
a park, preserve; [cf. मृग-कानन.]
—मृगया-
शील, अस्, आ, अम्, accustomed to the chase, attached
to hunting.
मृगयस्, आस्, m., Ved. a wild animal.

मृगयाण, अस्, आ, अम्, searching for, hunting
after, chasing, pursuing.

मृगयित्वा, ind. having searched, having investi-
gated.

मृगयु, उस्, m. a huntsman; a jackal; an epi-
thet of Brahmā.
मृगव, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.

मृगव्य, अम्, n. hunting, the chase; the butt
or mark in archery, a target.

मृगार, अस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns
Atharva-veda
